survey: An open envelope seen almost straight on, slightly turned so its right end is a little nearer the camera. The camera sits a little below the envelope. The front pocket is a rectangle: its left and right sides are vertical, and its bottom edge rises about 7° to the right. The right end is a bit taller than the left, and a rounded side and a thin bottom band show, which fits a near right end and a low camera. The open back flap rises behind as a triangle whose peak lines up roughly with the V-shaped cut of the pocket. A stack of three photos sits in the pocket. The front photo is upright with vertical sides, and its top edge runs at the same 7° as the envelope's bottom edge. The two photos behind it peek out to the right as narrow slivers that get smaller as they go back. The stamp and the postmark lie flat on the front face. The stamp's sides are vertical and its top and bottom follow the 7° edge direction, so it sits in the face's plane. The postmark circle is a mild ellipse, which suits a face seen nearly head-on. There is no separate ground plane, and the shadow sits evenly under the bottom edge.
